questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It allowed me to specialise my master's SUFONAMA in the area of conservation biology and landscape management. This gave me the opportunity to extend my expertise.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The second year SUFONAMA students did not fit in well into the master structure of the Conservation Biology and Landscape Management studies. There were periods of time where we had no courses, but also could not start with the thesis yet.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find the information. There was always staff you could contact and who helped fast and kind.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction events to find your way around the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy as there are many options. I used a website called "SpareRoom" and ended up moving in with two fellow students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is often cheaper to live off campus. All of the accommodations are small houses shared with often three other people. There can be very run-down places, be careful before and try to be sensitive about that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many options, both with different dorms, but also private housing off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Here is an example of SUFONAMA students not being considered enough. We were enrolled for all the courses of Conservation science and landscape management students, however, we were not supposed to attend all of them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Because I am a SUFONAMA student I was automatically enrolled for my courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was always possible to contact our tutor, or the responsible staff for our master.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was preregistered and got all my courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I cannot give much advice as I had a pre-organised master. Whoever will follow this master the only advise I have is to check that you haven't been registered for too many courses, as you don't have to take all of the courses in your second year.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
As the focus of the second year should have been "conservation and landscape management", this part fell short for SUFONAMA students. The course we had about conservation science was very basic in my opinion and I did not feel as if I could gain much knowledge. The same was for the Research planning and communication course where the focus was on less important knowledge. 
However, there were also many interesting and good things about the courses and I could take home new knowledge. Especially learning about R-studio and ArcGIS was very interesting and well made.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked the style of teaching. It was similar to UCPH: Small courses, approachable teachers, low hierarchy, many group projects, and excursions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Research Planning and Communication
Conservation Science
Agriculture and the Environment

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: I only wrote my Master Thesis here.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Conservation Science course gives a nice overview of what conservation is, both on the natural side and the human side.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Covid fees. To travel back into the UK tests had to be bought, which in the high phase of covid cost75 pound.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food generally was less expensive, especially compared with Denmark. I expected accommodation to be cheaper considering the small size of Bangor, but it turned out to be fairly expensive. Public Transport is very expensive in all of the UK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a society for everything at Bangor University.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are many societies, which fit your hobby perfectly. From every sport one can imagine to movie societies, game societies, cultural societies. 
Plus the short distance to Snowdonia National Park gives many hiking, climbing and biking opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going for many hikes in Snowdonia. It is for free and absolutely stunning.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Again, Snowdonia. But also go for a holiday to the south of Wales, or see nearby cities such as Conwy, LLandudno (Great Orme), go to Aberfalls and visit the distillery, Betws-y-Coed or many more. But also Chester, Liverpool and Manchester are close by.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to adjust to the culture. This comes however from a Germany person, where I feel like the culture in the UK is not far off.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I felt that people were very welcoming and friendly and appreciated talking to me. That made socializing easy. Societies always have a day of socials, were they organise activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The drinking and going-out culture. Many of the society events evolve around drinking. But that is off course something no one is forced to participate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendliness of people. It made it easy to feel welcomed and included.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Come weather prepared, with rain and windproof shoe wear and jackets. Field trips can get wet.
Don't be shy to approach staff and students, everyone is glad to help and talk to you.
If in any way possible a car is available, it is helpful to get around, especially in Snowdonia.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Winters can be long and rainy, so it is nice to plan trips with friends to keep up a good spirit. 
If you own them already, and like hiking, it is good to bring your gear.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met on the way turned out to be a great group if friends. Both in studies as well as in personal life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: As mentioned before I felt like the SUFONAMA second year at Bangor University was not well planned. That turned out to be very frustrating. Especially in the second semester, there were times where we had no courses, and no option to start our thesis, which left us with a long waiting period.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Since I am a Erasmus Mundus Master student, my experience is not the traditional exchange experience. Further I feel that an exchange during the Bachelor year would be better, as most students in Bangor are Bachelor students.
In my knowledge, the structure of SUFONAMA is to be changed. It is likely to be different in experiences of new students.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
